natural: like strangers passing on the road

meaning.en: To treat each other as strangers, though once close.
meaning.zh: 关系疏远，像不认识的路人一样。多指原来熟悉或亲近的人。

examples.zh: 两人吵翻之后形同陌路，再没说过一句话。
examples.en: After their quarrel the two became strangers and never spoke again.

examples.zh: 毕业十年，当年的室友如今形同陌路。
examples.en: Ten years after graduation, the old roommates have become strangers.

usage.en: Predicate. Describes people who were once close, such as friends, couples or relatives.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，指曾经亲近的朋友、夫妻、亲人等变得疏远。

antonyms: 海内存知己，天涯若比邻

natural: chasing fame and profit

meaning.en: To be obsessed with winning reputation and wealth.
meaning.zh: 一味追求名声和利益。

examples.zh: 他一生追名逐利，到头来却身边无人。
examples.en: He chased fame and profit all his life and ended up with no one beside him.

examples.zh: 她厌倦了职场里追名逐利的风气，决定回乡教书。
examples.en: Tired of the office culture of chasing status and money, she decided to go home and teach.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Usually critical.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常含批评。

synonyms: 世人都晓神仙好，惟有功名忘不了
antonyms: 别人笑我太疯癫，我笑他人看不穿

natural: treating the symptom, not the cause

meaning.en: To deal only with the surface of a problem and leave its cause untouched.
meaning.zh: 只解决表面问题，没有解决根本原因。

equivalents: treat the symptoms, not the disease

examples.zh: 多开几条路只是治标不治本，关键还是限制车辆总量。
examples.en: Building more roads only treats the symptom; the real fix is limiting the number of cars.

examples.zh: 加班赶进度治标不治本，流程不改，问题还会出现。
examples.en: Working overtime to catch up is a stopgap; unless the process changes, the problem will come back.

usage.en: Used of policies, measures and remedies. Often paired with 治本 (cure the root) or 标本兼治.
usage.zh: 多评论政策、措施、办法，常与“治本”“标本兼治”对举。

natural: every step is hard

meaning.en: To find it hard to make any progress, whether in walking or in a venture.
meaning.zh: 迈步都很困难，形容行动艰难，处境不顺。

examples.zh: 受债务拖累，这家公司举步维艰。
examples.en: Weighed down by debt, the company is struggling to move at all.

examples.zh: 大雪封山，救援队伍举步维艰。
examples.en: With the mountain blocked by snow, the rescue team could barely advance.

usage.en: Predicate. Applies to real walking and to business, reform or life situations.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，可指实际行走困难，也可指事业、改革、生活处境艰难。

natural: former grudges melting like ice

meaning.en: To let past grievances melt away completely and make up.
meaning.zh: 以前的怨恨像冰一样消融，彼此和好。

examples.zh: 经过一次长谈，兄弟俩终于冰释前嫌。
examples.en: After one long talk, the brothers finally buried the hatchet.

examples.zh: 两国领导人握手言欢，冰释前嫌。
examples.en: The two leaders shook hands and put their old quarrels behind them.

usage.en: Predicate. Usually describes two sides reconciling.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，指双方和好。

natural: slow to know, slow to realise

meaning.en: To be slow to understand or notice what is going on.
meaning.zh: 对事物的反应迟钝，事后才明白。

equivalents: be late to the penny dropping

examples.zh: 大家都看出他喜欢她了，只有她自己后知后觉。
examples.en: Everyone could see he liked her; only she was slow to catch on.

examples.zh: 我后知后觉，直到合同到期才发现条款有问题。
examples.en: I was slow on the uptake and only noticed the problem with the terms when the contract ran out.

usage.en: Often used humorously about oneself. Opposite of 先知先觉 (those who see ahead).
usage.zh: 常用来自嘲。与“先知先觉”相对。

natural: not telling good crops from weeds

meaning.en: To fail to tell good people or things from bad ones.
meaning.zh: 好的和坏的混在一起，不加区分。

equivalents: fail to separate the good from the bad

examples.zh: 网络平台良莠不分，家长要帮孩子筛选内容。
examples.en: Online platforms mix good and bad, so parents must help children filter content.

examples.zh: 这套教材良莠不分，需要重新编选。
examples.en: The textbook mixes the good with the bad and needs to be re-edited.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. 莠 is a weed that looks like millet (foxtail), hence the image.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。“莠”是一种形似谷子的杂草。

natural: utterly unknown

meaning.en: Not known to anyone; having no reputation at all.
meaning.zh: 没有名气，不为人所知。

examples.zh: 他曾是籍籍无名的小演员，一部戏后一举成名。
examples.en: He was an obscure bit-part actor until one film made him famous overnight.

examples.zh: 这位籍籍无名的作者，写出了年度畅销书。
examples.en: This unknown author wrote the bestseller of the year.

usage.en: Attributive or predicate. Often contrasts with sudden fame. 籍籍 is also written 藉藉 in old texts.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，常与一举成名对照。

natural: lost, then found again

meaning.en: To recover something that was lost.
meaning.zh: 丢失之后又重新得到。

examples.zh: 失而复得的钱包里，一分钱都没少。
examples.en: In the wallet that was lost and found again, not a penny was missing.

examples.zh: 走丢三天的小狗失而复得，全家喜出望外。
examples.en: The little dog, lost for three days, was found again, and the family was overjoyed.

usage.en: Attributive or predicate. Can apply to objects, people and opportunities.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，可指物品、人或机会。

natural: apply both kindness and authority

meaning.en: To combine generosity with strictness in governing or managing people.
meaning.zh: 既施恩惠，又显威严，宽严并用。

examples.zh: 好教练懂得恩威并施，既严格训练又关心队员。
examples.en: A good coach combines kindness with discipline, training hard and caring for the players.

examples.zh: 他对下属恩威并施，团队很听他的。
examples.en: He mixes warmth and strictness with his staff, and the team heeds him.

usage.en: Predicate. Describes managers, rulers, parents and teachers.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于领导、君主、家长、老师等。

natural: a long-buried wrong is cleared

meaning.en: For a long-standing injustice to be exposed and set right.
meaning.zh: 多年的冤屈终于得到洗清。

equivalents: be cleared of a long-standing wrong

examples.zh: 二十年后，这桩错案终于沉冤昭雪。
examples.en: Twenty years later the miscarriage of justice was finally put right.

examples.zh: 他在法庭上听到无罪判决，沉冤昭雪，泪流满面。
examples.en: Hearing the not-guilty verdict, his old wrong finally cleared, he wept.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Often used of wrongful convictions. Formal.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常用于冤案，较正式。

natural: one branch blooming alone

meaning.en: For one person or thing to stand out far above the rest, often leaving others behind.
meaning.zh: 一枝花独自开放，比喻一人或一事特别突出。

equivalents: stand head and shoulders above the rest

examples.zh: 这个行业不再是一枝独秀，新对手不断出现。
examples.en: The industry is no longer dominated by one player; new rivals keep emerging.

examples.zh: 她在全班一枝独秀，成绩远超第二名。
examples.en: She stood far ahead of the class, well beyond the runner-up.

usage.en: Predicate. Neutral; the tone depends on context. Often contrasted with 百花齐放.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。褒贬视语境而定，常与“百花齐放”对举。

natural: knowing it in heart and belly

meaning.en: To understand a matter perfectly well without needing to say it.
meaning.zh: 心里很清楚，不必明说。

equivalents: be perfectly aware without saying so

examples.zh: 这件事谁做的，大家心知肚明。
examples.en: Everyone knows perfectly well who did it.

examples.zh: 两人对彼此的心意心知肚明，只是谁也没挑明。
examples.en: Each knows full well how the other feels, but neither has spoken.

usage.en: Predicate. Often implies something both sides know but leave unsaid. Often with 都.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常含双方都明白却不说破之意，常与“都”连用。

pinyin: jīn guó bù ràng xū méi
natural: women are no less than men

meaning.en: Women are every bit as capable as men.
meaning.zh: 女子不比男子差。

equivalents: women are every bit as good as men
a woman's equal to any man

examples.zh: 这位女船长巾帼不让须眉，带队穿越了风暴区。
examples.en: The woman captain, every bit the equal of any man, led the crew through the storm zone.

examples.zh: 运动场上，姑娘们巾帼不让须眉。
examples.en: On the sports field the girls are the equal of the boys.

usage.en: Used in praise of women. Today some find it implies men are the standard, so it is often replaced by wording about equality. 巾帼 was a woman's headdress, 须眉 a man's beard and brows.
usage.zh: 用于称赞女性。“巾帼”指女子头饰，“须眉”指男子。如今有人认为以男性为标准，故也常改用平等的说法。

synonyms: 休言女子非英物，夜夜龙泉壁上鸣
身不得，男儿列，心却比，男儿烈

natural: a beauty is a flood of disaster

meaning.en: The old saying that a beautiful woman brings ruin on men or states.
meaning.zh: 旧时指美貌女子会给男人或国家带来灾祸。

examples.zh: 历史上总有人把亡国归咎于红颜祸水，其实是借口。
examples.en: Historians have often blamed a fallen state on a ruinous beauty, but that was an excuse.

examples.zh: 别再说什么红颜祸水了，错在他自己没有定力。
examples.en: Stop talking about a beauty bringing ruin; the fault was his own lack of self-control.

usage.en: Now mostly quoted in order to criticise it as a sexist trope that shifts blame onto women. Avoid using it of real people.
usage.zh: 今天多是为了批评这一把过错推给女性的陈旧偏见而提到。不宜用来指真人。

pinyin: zhì bù tóng dào bù hé
literal: aims · not · same · ways · not · fit
natural: different aims, ways that don't fit

meaning.en: If two people differ in aims and outlook, they cannot work together.
meaning.zh: 志向不同，主张不合，就无法共事。

examples.zh: 志不同道不合，他们终于各奔前程。
examples.en: With such different aims, they finally went their separate ways.

examples.zh: 合作两年后，志不同道不合，我们和平分手。
examples.en: After two years together, our aims and ways were too different, and we parted amicably.

usage.en: Often said when ending a partnership or friendship calmly. Folk saying; compare Confucius's 道不同，不相为谋.
usage.zh: 常用于平和地结束合作或友谊。民间说法，可参看《论语》“道不同，不相为谋”。

antonyms: 鱼找鱼，虾找虾，乌龟专找王八

natural: each nursing a secret scheme

meaning.en: For each of a group to harbour a hidden, selfish motive.
meaning.zh: 每个人都藏着不可告人的打算。

examples.zh: 联盟里各怀鬼胎，谁也不肯真心配合。
examples.en: The alliance members each have their own hidden agenda, and none will really cooperate.

examples.zh: 他们表面客气，实际各怀鬼胎。
examples.en: On the surface they are polite, but each has a secret plan.

usage.en: Predicate. Describes groups or partners, not a single person.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于一群人或合作各方。

natural: knowing shame is close to courage

meaning.en: To feel shame at one's faults and set about correcting them takes courage, or comes close to it.
meaning.zh: 懂得羞耻并改正错误，就接近于勇敢了。

equivalents: to feel shame is the first step to bravery

examples.zh: 知耻近乎勇，承认错误才有机会改正。
examples.en: Being ashamed is close to being brave; only by admitting a mistake can you fix it.

examples.zh: 老师说，知耻近乎勇，考砸了不要逃避，要找原因。
examples.en: The teacher said that facing your shame takes courage; don't avoid a bad result, find out why.

story.en: In the Doctrine of the Mean, Confucius says that love of learning is close to wisdom, vigorous practice is close to humaneness, and knowing shame is close to courage (子曰：好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇).
story.zh: 《中庸》载孔子说：“好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇。”

usage.en: Quoted when urging someone to own up and improve. Formal. The line belongs to a trio: 好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇.
usage.zh: 劝人认错改过时引用，较正式。原文是三句并列：好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇。

natural: the culprit files the complaint first

meaning.en: A wrongdoer accuses the victim first in order to shift the blame.
meaning.zh: 做了坏事的人抢先指责受害者，把责任推给别人。

equivalents: the guilty party cries foul first
the best defence is a good offence

examples.zh: 明明是他撞了人，还恶人先告状。
examples.en: He was the one who hit the person, yet he lodged the complaint first.

examples.zh: 遇到恶人先告状，要保留证据，冷静说明。
examples.en: If someone in the wrong accuses you first, keep your evidence and explain calmly.

usage.en: Predicate or comment on a situation. Casual; used of someone who blames others first.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或评论。口语，指倒打一耙的人。

synonyms: 猪八戒耍把式——倒打一耙
小偷击鼓进大堂——恶人先告状

pinyin: lì bá shān xī qì gài shì
literal: strength · pull up · mountain · oh · spirit · cover · world
natural: strength to uproot mountains, spirit to cover the world

meaning.en: Tremendous strength and a spirit that overshadows the whole world; the opening line of Xiang Yu's farewell song.
meaning.zh: 力量能拔起大山，气概压倒整个世界，形容英雄气概。出自项羽《垓下歌》。

examples.zh: 这位举重冠军力拔山兮气盖世，轻松举起了世界纪录的重量。
examples.en: The weightlifting champion, with strength to move mountains, easily lifted a world-record weight.

examples.zh: 读到“力拔山兮气盖世”，仿佛看见西楚霸王的豪迈。
examples.en: Reading 'strength to uproot mountains, spirit to cover the world', one seems to see the Hegemon-King's bravado.

story.en: Surrounded at Gaixia, Xiang Yu sang: 'My strength uprooted mountains, my spirit covered the world; but the times are against me and my horse Zhui will not run' (力拔山兮气盖世，时不利兮骓不逝).
story.zh: 项羽被困垓下，悲歌慷慨：“力拔山兮气盖世，时不利兮骓不逝。”

usage.en: Often quoted in its short form 力拔山兮, usually to praise physical strength or heroic spirit. The next line, 时不利兮骓不逝, tells of his defeat, so it can also carry a tragic tone.
usage.zh: 常只引“力拔山兮”，用来赞叹力量或英雄气概。下句“时不利兮骓不逝”写败局，所以也可带悲壮色彩。

synonyms: 鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳——力大无穷

natural: when the person leaves, the tea goes cold

meaning.en: Once someone loses their position, the courtesy and influence they enjoyed vanish.
meaning.zh: 人一离开原来的位置，别人对他的热情和他的影响力也随之消失。

equivalents: out of sight, out of mind
fall from favour and be forgotten

examples.zh: 他退休不到一年，就深感人走茶凉。
examples.en: Less than a year after retiring, he felt keenly that the warmth had gone with his job.

examples.zh: 官场上人走茶凉，是常有的事。
examples.en: In officialdom, being forgotten once you leave your post is common.

usage.en: A comment on fickle social ties. Often said with resignation.
usage.zh: 感叹世态炎凉，常带无奈。

natural: to buy people's hearts

meaning.en: To win people's support by favours, gifts or promises, usually with a selfish motive.
meaning.zh: 用恩惠、钱财或许诺来争取人们的拥护。

examples.zh: 他发放红包不过是收买人心。
examples.en: His handing out of cash gifts was nothing but a bid to buy loyalty.

examples.zh: 新官上任先减税，被批评是收买人心。
examples.en: The new official cut taxes straight away and was criticised for buying support.

usage.en: Predicate; usually critical, implying insincere motives.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常含批评，暗示动机不纯。

natural: petty theft

meaning.en: Petty stealing of small items.
meaning.zh: 偷一些不值钱的小东西的行为。

examples.zh: 他从小就有小偷小摸的毛病，家长必须及时管教。
examples.en: He has had a habit of petty thieving since childhood, and his parents must correct it in time.

examples.zh: 商场里小偷小摸的事，保安见得多了。
examples.en: Security guards at the mall have seen plenty of petty pilfering.

usage.en: Used for habitual minor theft, not for serious crime. Can be an attributive.
usage.zh: 指惯偷小东西，不指严重犯罪。可作定语。
